Exposure weights of the immediate-treatment estimator in a stepped-wedge design

Source: R/stepped_wedge.R
sw_exposure_weights.Rd

Computes the implicit exposure-time weights \(W_e\), \(e = 1, \ldots, T-1\), of the immediate-treatment (IT) estimator, so that \(E(\hat\beta) = \sum_e W_e \theta_e\) under exposure-time heterogeneity. The weights sum to one.

Usage

sw_exposure_weights(
  design,
  phi = NULL,
  icc = NULL,
  cac = 1,
  m = NULL,
  estimator = c("GLS", "TWFE"),
  sizes = NULL
)

Arguments

design

numeric vector of length T: cluster counts (or shares) for start periods 2, ..., T, followed by the number wait-listed. The first entry must be positive.

phi

Hussey–Hughes parameter \(\phi = m\rho/(1-\rho)\) (GLS); Inf gives the fixed-effects limit.

icc, cac, m

alternative nested-exchangeable specification: within-period ICC, cluster autocorrelation and individuals per cluster-period (see [sw_phi_nested()]). With sizes, m is not needed.

estimator

"GLS" (default) or "TWFE" (two-way fixed effects, which does not use the covariance).

sizes

optional G x T matrix of cluster-period sizes, one row per cluster in design order (sequence 2 first, wait-list last). Requires integer counts in design and, for GLS, icc and cac.

Value

named numeric vector W1, ..., W(T-1)

Examples

sw_exposure_weights(c(6, 6, 6, 6, 0), phi = 2)          # complete wedge
#>          W1          W2          W3          W4 
#>  0.94285714  0.30000000 -0.07142857 -0.17142857 
sw_exposure_weights(c(4, 4, 4, 4, 8), phi = 2)          # 8 wait-listed
#>          W1          W2          W3          W4 
#>  0.67058824  0.30000000  0.06470588 -0.03529412 
sw_exposure_weights(c(6, 6, 6, 6, 0), estimator = "TWFE")
#>   W1   W2   W3   W4 
#>  1.0  0.3 -0.1 -0.2
